title.narrative: Strengthening RUTF pipeline for life-saving nutrition interventions for children under 5 in the BAY States of Northeast Nigeria

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project will provide lifesaving humanitarian assistance for the management of children under five years of age with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) in 6 Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Borno, Adamawa Yobe (BAY) States of northeastern Nigeria through the provision of a continuous supply of lifesaving ready to use therapeutic foods (RUTF.ltbrgtMalnutrition is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality of children aged 6-59 months old, and the risk of death is nine times higher than that of children without it. In line with UNICEF’s strategic intent to support governments and partners to deliver nutrition services, UNICEF will provide technical and financial support to the State Primary Health Care Development Agencies in the BAY States and partners using resources from the Swedish International Development Cooperation (SIDA), Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), BMZ and Global Affairs Canada (GAC) to deliver nutrition services to most in-need children in the BAY states. As the sole provider of RUTF to the partners in northeast Nigeria and the sector provider of last resort (PoLR), UNICEF will use the resources from CERF to ensure an uninterrupted supply pipeline of RUTF in the target locations. With support from multiple donors, the supply pipeline is secured until mid-February 2024. ltbrgtUNICEF, therefore, seeks USD 600,000 to reach 10,000 vulnerable children (5,400 girls and 4,600 boys) 6–59 months with SAM in 6 LGAs in the BAY states to reduce malnutrition, morbidity, and mortality. UNICEF will procure and preposition RUTF supplies only with this assistance. Additionally, 10,000 indirect beneficiaries, primarily caregivers of children with SAM, will receive nutrition counselling.ltbrgtlt/pgt
